en: We are finally here.\n*Sigh*...

It sounds like there's
something more you want
to say...not that I want to
hear it.
That is a terrible thing to\nsay! Are you devoid of any\nsympathy!?

All right, all right. If you're
so desperate for someone
to listen, I will hear you
out.
Thank you. I want to talk\nto you about that\nthing―the thornite.

I have been running
analysis after analysis, but
regardless of what
methodology I employ, I
am unable to draw any
concrete conclusions.

That means if these
creatures are really the
Purge's creation, they
possess some very
advanced technology.

Exactly. Their knowledge
likely far surpasses ours!
We have no chance of
defeating them...
The captain is right.\nMoping will get us\nnowhere.
We will be relying on you\nmore than ever before,\nCoro.
Then I have no choice but\nto live up to your\nexpectations!

Come thornites or rebels, I
will find a way to
overcome anything that
obstructs our path
forward!
With that in mind, I shall\nbestow upon this planet\nthe name <font color=yellow>Dvaleor</font>!
(I really am good. Coro\ntook the bait.)

Nothing on this planet
even remotely resembles
a city. The civilization here
is likely in its very early
stages.
Have you noticed any\nunderground cavities?
Yes.
...So this place, too, has\nbeen tainted by the\nplague that is the Purge.
Or perhaps not. There are\nmany caverns, but they\nare all very small in scale.
What does that mean?
Maybe the Purge is in the\nmiddle of excavations!
I guess they're formations\nunrelated to the Purge.
...This must be the hole\nexperience. Hehe.
Impossible!

You think the cavities are
small because they are in
the process of syphoning
resources!?

If that is true, that means
some of the Purge
members are on this
planet.
Wait.

It doesn't make sense. A
primitive civilization such
as this one would be
incapable of creating such
cavities.
You certainly make a good\npoint.
This is the work of the\nPurge. We must keep our\nguards up.
Captain...
You have just unleashed\nupon us a restricted Class\nB symbology spell...
...The Dad Joke.

The Dad Joke!? I am
unfamiliar with that
symbology. What does it
do?

It dampens the mood of
the room and causes
people to die a little on
the inside.
C-captain, what―
No!!! Don't!
This ends here! Ask any\nmore questions, and you'll\nlose your soul.

If you are so desperate to
become as soulless as the
captain, however, I will not
stop you.
Do not worry, Eve! I-I shall\nstay far away from the\nsubject!
At long last we have\ncaught up to the Purge\nmembers!
We must us land quickly\nor they might get away!
Understood! Commencing\nlanding sequence!

It is truly astonishing!
Extraordinary, even! What
is the phrase I am looking
for again?
Ah, yes! We have received\nheaven's pennies!

You mean "pennies from
heaven," right? Not that I
would have used that
particular phrase to
describe our luck...
Let us not sweat the\ndetails.

The pennies to which I
refer is the pulse tower
before us. We landed right
in front of it!
Huh!?
That really is quite\nincredible...
Indeed. The only fitting\nterm would be "miracle."

The probability of us
landing in this exact spot
is astronomical! In fact, I
would estimate it close to
our chances of returning
to Earth.
...Dear lord! Is the\npossibility of us making it\nback truly so slim!?

The future looks grim.
...That is assuming we
even have a future!
Perhaps we are fated to
turn to corpses in space
and become gh-ghosts―

M-my apologies! You are
correct. We must focus on
the task before our very
eyes first.
To learn more about the\nexcavations, we need to\nbring our sensors back up.
Let us quickly go and shut\ndown the pulse tower.

I have confirmed that the
tower is down and our
sensors are back online. I
shall be awaiting your
return.
Wait. Look over there!\nThere's a person standing\nin that boulder's shadow!
(I've been noticed!)
We have no intention to\nhurt you! We just want to\ntalk.

Aaah! P-please have
mercy! God, Buddah,
Towerlord above―please,
save me!
I-I am but a low-ranking\nLevarance citizen. I have\nnothing of value!

I'm only here because I
was brought to this place
by our supreme leader
<font color=yellow>Eldram</font>!
Supreme leader!? Who is\nthis individual you speak\nof?
I am worthless! My life\nmeans very little―please\njust let me go!

<font color=yellow>Terry</font>, why are you hiding
in the shadows? Are you
guys playing
hide-and-seek?
Quiet, <font color=yellow>Kurt</font>! This isn't a\ngood time!
Ugh! I can't believe you're\nplayin' without me!
Kurt? Is that your name?\nMight we talk to you for a\nmoment?
Huh? Who're you?

Captain, we have an
emergency on our hands!
There is a group of armed
individuals nearby!
Oooh! That's one of 'em\nrobot things, right? Look,\nTerry―it's adorable!
Relief is here! Kurt, forget\nthe robot.
We need to go find <font color=yellow>Val</font>!

B-but I like it so much.
...And these people also
say they wanna talk with
us.
We want nothing to do\nwith pirates―come on!
Ouch! My arm! Don't pull\non it!
...And off they go...
There wasn't even enough\ntime to ask them one\nquestion.
You're right! We need to\nleave this place before\nthe troops arrive!

Allow me to begin
calculating an escape
route. We must leave
posthaste!

Captain, Eve―welcome
back. I am glad to see you
managed to return without
incident.

Yes, but sadly we are
none the wiser from our
excursion. Those two ran
off before we could gain
any information.

There was nothing that
could be done. Let us
count our blessings. Your
safety is far more
important than mere data.

Besides, this result is to
be expected. After all, if I
did not know you, and you
attempted to talk to me
with that look in your
eyes, I would run away,
too.
Eek!

W-wait! Please have mercy
on this loveable AI!
Violence is not the best
way to solve problems!

Indeed! No doubt there
are nuggets of vital
knowledge hidden in the
short conversation you
had.

It appears this individual
called Eldram brought
people to this planet and
is using them as forced
labor.

Levarance is a
dictatorship so there is a
good chance that is the
case.
They're using these poor\nsouls to steal other\nplanets' resources!
A moment, if you would!\nThere is one other thing\nyou are forgetting...
One more thing?
That boy Kurt said I am\nadorable!
He has impeccable taste.
...Unlike certain individuals\nwho shall remain unnamed.
Hmph. Come, Captain―we\nmust continue our\ninvestigations posthaste!
No! Wait! Please do not\nignore me! You are hurting\nmy feelings!

Additionally, I think you
would be pleased to hear
that I have followed Kurt's
route and discovered
something interesting.
Something interesting?
Yes. I have detected a\nlarge-scale mining\noperation.

That's right. Perhaps we
will be able to gain some
more information on the
Purge here!
Indeed.

From what I gleaned of
Terry and Kurt's
conversation, there are a
lot of Levarance citizens
who are not happy with
their current situation and
are possibly even looking
to rebel.

With a bit more prodding,
we should be able to get
them to divulge all they
know about the Purge.

Yes. It is certainly
possible. I must ask,
however, that you move
with the utmost caution
when conducting such
probing.
To think that there would\nbe thornites... Are the two\nof you all right?
We are fine, thanks to the\ncaptain.

Hey! Are either of you
hurt!? That was a real
close call―they nearly had
us.

Nearly had us...? The
captain was fighting the
beasts while you were
cowering behind the
boulder!
You make it sound like\nyou were in the fray with\nus!

Hahaha! It's about the
support―whether in spirit
or body it doesn't matter
so much! What's important
is that we help each
other!
Is he even listening to\nwhat he's saying...?
Val! Are you okay!?
Sorry we ran away...
You!!!
Oh! You're the people from\nearlier―the tower vandals!
Don't call them that!\nThere's no way these guys\nare vandals!

I have faced death with
these two individuals―they
are the truest of true
friends. Insult them, and I'll
never forgive you!
Again, you did nothing.\nYou were hiding behind a\nrock the whole time.

Ah, yes. Now that we're
the truest of true friends,
maybe we can ask you a
few questions.

What is it? Is something
troubling you? Go ahead―I
would be more than happy
to help.

So even the people of
Levarance consider
thornites to be mysterious
creatures...

That reminds me, we were
attacked by those beasts
at the base once. We
barely escaped with our
lives.

My mother said there
weren't any when she was
young. They only started
appearing these past few
years.

So does that mean in part
of the galaxy, something
occurred during the past
few years to give rise to
the thornites?

...We do not know―you
would probably have to
ask the planet's
researchers to learn the
answer to that.
Well, there's been one big\nchange. Lord Eldram's\nbecomin' leader.

What are you taking
about, Kurt? How is that
at all related to the
planet's ecosystem?
You're right. Sorry.

There is no need to
apologize. If you don't
mind, could you tell us
more about him?

Can you explain the
current regime to us, what
the goal of "Operation:
Frost," and why you are
mining resources?
That's a whole lot of\nquestions!
I am not sure I have\nanswers to any of them...
Do you know of anyone\nwho would?

All the people here are
commoners like us... They
probably know only about
as much as we do.
...What 'bout that device\nat the warehouse?
While it's a little\nold-school, it should still\nwork!

Yes! Also considering
that's where all the
rubbish goes, there should
be no guards around. Kurt,
why don't you show them
there?
Hey, Coro! Coro! Did I do a\ngood job?
Of course you did!\nThanks for your help,\nKurt.
Now could you give us\nthe route to the\nwarehouse?
Of course! We're lifelong\nfriends, after all!
Well, what are we waiting\nfor? Let's go!
We've finally made it!
So you use emptied mines\nas storage spaces?

...Or should I say landfills?
According to my scans of
the interior, this place has
not been in use recently.
What of the security\nsystems?
They are in functioning\norder―just powered down.
From what I can see this\nplace is being guarded by\nprimitive creatures.

Do you think the devices
in there are really still
working? They haven't
exactly put a lot of effort
into maintaining the
security of this area.
Indeed. It is far from the\nbest.
...According to Val, Eldram\nhas all of Levarance under\nhis thumb.
He is the\nbe-all-end-all―the sole\nruler.

That means so long as we
can stop him, we can put
an end to this mining
operation.
I fully agree!

I just have to wonder, how
is it possible for one
person to gain so much
power?
Maybe the device will have\nsome answers for us.
Well, he is a pretty shady\ncharacter...
He just must be really\ngood at his job!
I hope so. Instead of\nstanding here and talking,\nlet's move forward then.

We must learn everything
we can about Eldram, his
plans, rare metals, and
mining!

That is true. After all, we
are talking about a man
who refuses to have a
right-hand man or confide
his plans in anyone but
himself.
He must be an incredibly\nlonely person...
...Not that that excuses\nany of his actions.
Far from it!

The man has disregarded
his people's rights, other
civilizations' rights, and
has been making decisions
that impact everyone
without any consideration
for anyone but himself.
Good at his job!? I beg to\ndisagree!
Yes! Eve is right!

On our ship, we take
everyone's opinions into
account before deciding
our course of action.
Captain, you are far\nbetter at your job than he\nis!
You really like <player>,\ndon't you?
Come on, let's go now.

Yes, but please do be
careful! Remember there
are dangerous beasts
guarding the warehouse!

I've found it! I've found
the device. Can you
connect me to the bridge
system?
You guys! Thank god\nyou're safe!
Wh-what are you doing\nhere!?

We asked everyone else
and they told us that the
beasts dwelling here are
extremely deadly.
We were worried about\nyou.
I'm glad to see that while\nyou look battered, you are\nat least safe.
...Thank you for thinking\nabout us.

Now that everyone is
here, let us see what
information we can gather
from this device.
<font color=green>Operation: Frost</font>―a plan\nby Adel Kleiman.

Many have been falling
victim to the <font color=yellow>Devil's
Plague</font>. Operation: Frost is
expected to decrease the
number of casualties.

Those who have not been
infected by the virus will
be sent to a distant
planet. The diseased
planet will undergo
supercooling.

I heard about this from my
father once. He told me
that the Devil's Plague
was an extremely
contagious disease...

In just two years after the
first person was infected,
nearly half of Levarance
had fallen victim to it.
Nearly half!? That most\ncertainly qualifies as\nextremely contagious.

That was over 80 years
ago. The planet is still
supercooled...and the
infected people along with
it.

Those who were lucky
enough to avoid
contracting the virus were
sent to live at one of the
seven satellite bases.

They were unable to find
a cure or a means to
quarantine it. That is why
they resorted to this.
It seems like there is still\nsome more. Please\ncontinue reading.

<font color=green>Revival of the Devil's
Plague</font> We have confirmed
that an individual in
Sector A of the space
station has contracted
the virus.

The government has
issued a directive to
eliminate this sector. It will
undergo supercooling.
I remember it like it was\nyesterday...

Sector A was where the
central government
operated. Many of the
most important people
died first.

And am I right in assuming
it was Eldram that helped
to quell the panic that
followed?

No. He came out of
nowhere and began
pushing to not only
supercool Sector A but
the entire planet with it.

So Eldram supercooled all
the highest government
executives, and in doing
so, became the central
authority.

Shortly after that, even
areas that were vaguely
suspected of having the
plague were supercooled,
along with any opposition
forces.

Everyone lived in constant
fear that they would be
next. Most people were so
afraid they couldn't even
sleep.

It weren't long before they
ran out of energy to
continue operations.
That's when they started
sendin' us to collect rare
metals.

And that is what caused
the imbalance in the
ecosystems of the planets
that were mined,
eventually leading to their
destruction.
Wh-what do you mean\nplanets were destroyed!?

You don't know? The
pulse tower mining
operations are destroying
planets from the core.

We have seen so many
neighboring planets, which
have been completely
devastated. To start with...
I cannot believe it...

To think that so many
people on so many planets
had to suffer because of
us...
Aaaaaah! What have we\ndone!? AAAAAAAAAH!!!
V-Val!?
It is terrible to think that\nwe pushed these other\nplanets to their limits...

Aaaaaah! I will find a way
to make up for everything
we have done, even if it
costs my life!

Please don't die! Your life
should not be something
you throw away so easily.
Captain, please tell him!

So my death will do
nothing for anyone? How,
then, can I undo all the
wrong!?
You can fight alongside us\nto dispose of Eldram.
...You wanna fight Lord\nEldram?

What you're asking of us
is very difficult. To go
against him would mean
putting our friends and
family in danger.
I could never betray my\nfriends...

To think that if even one
person were to revolt,
everyone here will be
punished... That is a very
precarious position to be
in.
Yes. In giving us a map of\nthis planet, you have\nalready helped us plenty.
I'm gald to hear that we\nwere able to assist you in\nsome way―however small.
Yes, we will see that it is\nused to its full potential.
I will begin searching for\nmore locations using the\nmap.

Captain, I am still
searching for devices
similar to the one we
found at the warehouse.

Sounds like this may take
some time. While we are
waiting for Coro, perhaps
we should review the large
volume of information we
gathered.
Understood!
Let's start with <font color=green>the\nPurge's goals</font>.

Eighty years ago,
Levarance was overtaken
by the <font color=yellow>Devil's Plague</font>,
which quickly turned into
a pandemic.

...Thus <font color=yellow>Operation: Frost</font>
was born, and the planet
was supercooled to
prevent the virus from
spreading any further. It
was a success.

A few years ago, however,
the virus reemerged at
the main government
base. Many top officials
were lost to the disease.
It was from the following\nchaos that <font color=yellow>Lord Eldram</font>\nemerged.
He used the people's fear\nto his advantage and\nappointed himself leader.

Anyone who dared oppose
him was mercilessly
supercooled along with
the base.
All that supercooling,\nhowever, required a great\ndeal of energy.

Yes, and in order to
procure that amount of
power they resorted to
using <font color=yellow>pulse towers</font>.

These towers modify the
soils to produce <font color=yellow>rare
metals</font>, which are used for
supercooling.
That's not all they\nproduce.

Pulse towers also emit
magnetic jamming waves
that <font color=green>damage the host
planet's core and cause
their ecosystems to go
haywire</font>.

Even if they did it to
protect their own planet,
these transgressions
cannot be forgiven!

Yes, but it sounds as
though many of them were
unaware of the
consequences their
actions had on these
planets.
That is true... Talking to\nthose three did change\nmy views somewhat...

You are right. The people
in the recordings on
Pasithee appeared to be
aware of the danger the
three pulse towers on
their planet posed.
Indeed. They even\nreferred to them as the\ndevil's instruments...
Their pleas likely never\nreached the people of\nLevarance.
The search results are in!\nI have located another\ndevice!

Unfortunately, the area it
is in appears to be under
heavy security―similar to
that at the mining sites.

There might even be some
Purge officers on patrol.
Perhaps we should forget
about this?

The fact that security is
so tight means something
there is worth protecting,
right?

I strongly believe going
there will allow us to gain
more information on
Eldram and the Purge.
Captain, don't you think\nthe potential reward is\nworth the risk?

Exactly! This might even
give us a chance to
convince some more
people!
Convince people to what?
To help us put an end to\nOperation: Frost.

They must know things
need to change. We have
to inform of the terrible
effect their actions have
had on other planets.

That is a great idea! It
would be unfair to judge
and punish them for
something they were not
aware they were doing.
Indeed. As they say, hate\nthe sin but not the sinner.
Now let's go and see if we\ncan't talk some sense into\nthese officers!
Wh-who the hell are you!?
We are not here to harm\nyou. We simply want to\ntalk.
You are a Purge official,\nright?
Y-you know who we are!?\nThis must be reported\nimmediately!
Please listen to us―even if\nit's just for a moment.
Wh-what!?
It is so dark! So scary!\nPlease help me!!!
Why are you afraid?\nYou're back at the ship!\nIt's not even dark there.
Ah, that's right.
I will begin calculating an\nescape route. Please\nreturn here immediately.
I prayed for your safe\nreturn.
What was all that about?\nIt suddenly went dark.

I do not know. There do
not appear to be any
issues with power
transmission...
Perhaps they called for\nbackup.
Maybe they were decoys?
It must be their bedtime!

Ah, so they powered down
certain sections to allow
their officers to safely
escape.
That sounds awfully\nlow-tech...

Sometimes it is the
low-tech things that are
the most effective, even in
highly advanced
civilizations.

Well, considering how
much it scared you, I
suppose you might be
right...

They likely powered down
the area to induce
confusion and use that to
escape.
So we were tricked!?
Well, that is one theory...
If that were the case,\nturning back will do us no\ngood.
Then we should call it a\nday, too! Let us brush our\nteeth and head to bed!

The working conditions
here are not exactly ideal.
We must take extra care
to keep our bodies in
shape, as they are our
number one asset!

I suggest we begin
improving our lifestyle by
setting a designated
lights-out time.
Captain, you have\nexcellent eyes!
I really don't think that's\nthe case...

Regardless, we must
assume that our presence
on this planet has been
revealed to our enemies.

The pulse tower going
down alone would have
been enough to tip them
off.
We must operate with\ngreat discretion from here\non out.
Yes. When you next go\nout to gather information,\nplease use caution.

I am terribly sorry,
Captain! I have lost the
signals of the Purge
officers!
But our sensors are\nworking, right? We shut\ndown the tower.
The sensors suddenly\nwent haywire and the\nsignals just disappeared.

Are you sure you didn't
lose track of them
because you were playing
games while on duty
again?

Multitasking is my forte!
Even if I were playing
games, I never would have
lost them.
Um...
So you were playing\ngames!?
Er―well... Uh...
...Not you, too, Captain?
I-I am terribly sorry!\nPlease do not glare at me\nin that manner!

You see, I could not stop. I
was in the middle of an
intense boss battle. I told
myself, if I won then I
could even ask a girl out.
...Then again, if we do not\nfind a way back to Earth, I\nwill not be able to do that.

Regardless, playing
against an enemy at full
CPU was incredibly
satisfying. The storyline
that followed was also
incredible!
Ah! I am terribly sorry!

I do not know how I lost
them... I think there is a
good chance they noticed
they were being tracked.
Do not try to shift\nresponsibility!
*Sob*

It is not all bad news,
though! In the area where
their signals disappeared, I
discovered an unguarded
warehouse.
It is very similar to the\none we were at earlier.

While this does not make
up for your earlier
mistake, at least it's
something.
Do you think there is\nanother one of those\ndevices there?
Yes. I checked and\ndouble-checked nine times\njust to be sure.

What do you say,
Captain? Should we forget
about those officers for
now and go take a look at
this place?
Please be careful! It also\nappears to have become a\nsafe haven for creatures.
...It really is similar to the\nlast place, but not in a\ngood way.

I agree! Regardless of how
many or what kind of
enemies we may face, not
going is not an option.

Besides, now that we are
aware of the dangers, we
will be going in with both
our eyes open!

The device should be in
this area, right? Coro,
could you give us more
precise coordinates?
Coro, are you playing\ngames again!? We need a\nresponse!
...Our communication has\nbeen dropped? What in\nthe world is going on...?
Coro, answer us! Coro?\nCORO!
...It's no use. Your ship is\nunder our command.
You're that man! The\nguerrilla leader from\nFarbrooke... You must be...
Eldram!

The one and only. And you
must be the intruders
heckling my workers and
running about attempting
to gather information.
For how long have I\nknown?
Since you landed on this\nplanet.
You knew this entire time\nand did not try to stop\nus?
Why would I?
I could squash you like the\ninsects you are at any\nmoment, if I so wished.
W-we're completely\nsurrounded!?
...Is this the end?

They're all around us, and
our ship has been taken
hostage. How are we
going to get out of this?
Wh-what's happening!?

There has been an
explosion in the
warehouse! The cause is
unknown but the barrels
of gunpowder inside have
caught fire and the flames
are out of control!
Eek!
This shabby ol' place is\ngonna go up in flames!

Look! Their formation has
been broken. Let's use
this opportunity to
escape!

No!!! You're not getting
away! Lord Eldram, do not
worry. We will have them
tracked.
Let them go.
Wh-what do you mean!?
They are but specks in\nthe cosmos. They pose no\nthreat to us.
*Pant* *Pant* We somehow\nescaped...
...But how are we going to\nget Coro and our ship\nback?
Talk about a close call! I'm\nso glad we made it in time!
That was more than a\nclose call! We nearly died\nback there!
Wait. That explosion... Was\nthat you?
You bet it was!
What about you and your\nfriends!? Opposing him\nwould mean―
Don't worry. We have their\nsupport.

We told everyone what
was happening on the
other planets and we've all
decided to rebel together!
But...!
If we don't stand up and\nfight, nothing will change.

Exactly. Besides, living
every day in fear does not
suit me! As a man of
honor, it is my job to
strike out against
injustice!

We're going to go back
and join the others. You
guys had better hurry
back to your ship.
But what about you...!?
They're gone... I wonder if\nthey'll be okay...

If we remain here, Val and
our other friends' efforts
will have been in vain. We
must trust they have
everything under control
and run while we still can.
